note: Curated catalog of open source video generation models, restricted to unconditionally free licenses only (Apache-2.0/MIT, no custom "community license", no MAU/revenue thresholds, no academic-only caveats). Verified via web search Aug 2026. Model ids are Hugging Face repo ids intended for DiffusionPipeline.from_pretrained. VRAM figures are sourced from model cards/community benchmarks and vary with resolution/frame count/offloading; treat as approximate. Deliberately excluded despite being otherwise capable: ByteDance Waver 1.0 (not open-weight at all), MiniMax-H3 (license bars local deployment in the US/EU/UK/South Korea), AnimateDiff (README says "academic use" despite an Apache-2.0 tag), LTX-Video/LTX-2.5 (LTX Community License: free only under $10M revenue, bars training competing AI systems, bars competing products), CogVideoX-5B (CogVideoX License: requires commercial registration, capped at 1M visits/month), HunyuanVideo-1.5 (Tencent Community License: free only under 100M MAU).

minimal.description: Entry-level/laptop GPU. No model in this catalog fits below 8GB now that AnimateDiff (academic-use license) is excluded.

low.description: Single consumer GPU, e.g. RTX 3060/4060/4070 class.

mid.description: High-end consumer/prosumer GPU, e.g. RTX 4090/5090, L4/L40S class.

high.description: Datacenter GPU or multi-GPU, e.g. A100/H100 80GB class.

magi_1_distilled.notes: Autoregressive chunk-based generation (predicts fixed-length video chunks sequentially, next chunk starts before current fully denoises) rather than single-shot diffusion — designed to hold up better over longer/more dynamic motion than same-tier single-shot models. 12GB figure requires window_size=1 in the distill+quant config.

wan2.1_1.3b.notes: Smallest member of the Wan family, explicitly built for consumer GPUs.

cogvideox_2b.notes: Smaller sibling of CogVideoX-5B — note the 5B is under the restrictive custom CogVideoX License, but the 2B was relicensed to Apache-2.0. Trained in FP16; quantizable further with PytorchAO/Optimum-quanto down to free-tier-Colab-class GPUs.

wan2.2_ti2v_5b.notes: Unified T2V+I2V in one checkpoint. ~27.4GB at FP16 for 25 frames @ 768x512; FP8 cuts ~40%. Very fast — a 5s 720p clip in under 9 minutes on a single consumer GPU. Currently the only mid-tier model in this catalog.

wan2.2_a14b.params: 27B total / 14B active per step (MoE: high-noise + low-noise experts)
wan2.2_a14b.notes: First open source MoE video model. Default requires an 80GB-class GPU (A100/H100); --offload_model/--t5_cpu flags trade speed for lower VRAM but 80GB is the no-compromise figure.

mochi_1.notes: Very strong motion quality/coherence. ~60-70GB single-GPU at full precision for the full 163-frame length; the bf16 variant with ComfyUI-level optimization can run under 22GB, at reduced frame count/speed.

skyreels_v1.notes: Fine-tuned from HunyuanVideo on ~10M film/TV clips; best open option for human-centric cinematic quality (faces, expression, camera work).

magi_1_full.notes: Full, non-distilled version. Exact VRAM floor not confirmed via search; scaling from the 4.5B variant's ~24GB at standard precision implies an 80GB+ class requirement. Same autoregressive chunk-based architecture as magi_1_distilled, at full quality.

ugc_product_review.note: Use each model's image-to-video variant, conditioned on reference_image, when product fidelity matters.

commercial_product_ad.note: Use each model's image-to-video variant, conditioned on reference_image, when product fidelity matters.

presenter_avatar.note: No freely-licensed model in this catalog does native dialogue/audio. These produce a silent video only; dialogue/voice_tone are not fulfilled by generation itself.

social_short_form_ad.note: Produces the silent visual only. Same caveat as presenter_avatar applies if dialogue is required.

music_video.note: No freely-licensed model in this catalog supports native audio-video sync — LTX-2.5 was the only one and its license isn't unconditionally free. This type currently has no viable pick.

motion_graphics.note: No model in this catalog targets abstract/graphic motion-design output; entries here are the fastest-iteration fallback, not a genuine fit.
